issue.title: [Canonical #21; blocks #11] DOC-native 3D game and generated WGSL
issue.body:
## Migration record — 2026-11-25

Original development mirror: https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/3. Canonical requirements and historical evidence remain at their original URLs. The new development/CI target is https://github.com/x0796666-ui/doc2; exact source history import is pending authentication. Original state: closed.

---

## Accepted — 2026-11-24
Exact accepted revision: [fcedb889915ea86f8476dc8c2b4f5b341cd97087](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/fcedb889915ea86f8476dc8c2b4f5b341cd97087).
- [Native Linux validation](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45347136352): CPU and software WebGPU both successful. 17 real X11 surface presentations, keyboard/resize, CPU parity, separate offscreen readback; 16 automatic mixed frontiers of 9 CPU + 134 GPU states; independent and dependent specialized generated WGSL pipelines, cache reuse. Actual source mutation, two depth draw orders, three face light levels, 1200 covered pixels, 56718 mutated pixels, jump=24 then landed=0, 16 repeat renders and two rejected malformed inputs. Typed checkpoint/WAV/replay/worker parity and failure-atomic invalid projection tests.
- [Physical exact-SHA Kaggle validation](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45347868118): successful; [raw artifact](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45347868118/artifacts/14898263862) independently inspected. Exact native CI bundle SHA provenance; Tesla T4 DiscreteGpu vendor 4318 device 7864; 17 full 3D CPU/physical frames identical, 1424 CPU + 2144 GPU nodes, 16 mixed frontiers, 134 states per dispatch across 3 workgroups, 15 generated pipeline cache hits after first compile. Actual game mesh proof on physical GPU: covered=1200 mutated=56718 lighting=3 depth_orders=2 jump=24 landed=0 repeats=16 rejected=2; injected dispatch failure retains initial frame only. 42 signed GPU episodes, 62 DOC-source cases, 27 benchmark samples. Physical rendering is offscreen, not a physical desktop surface. Prior 2D regression same-device CPU p50/p95 1463/1659 us RSS 4456 KiB; automatic physical mixed p50/p95 5466/456854 us RSS 324468 KiB; no speedup claim. 
- DOC authors game, typed scene, mesh/material/camera/lighting, pure scalar generated compute and render expressions; native host supplies generic platform ABI, presentation and I/O. Bounded fixed-point mesh shader subset, no arbitrary GPU effect admission, synchronous frame resource retirement. Legacy 2D handwritten shader remains regression-only in scope, legacy compute encoder/shader not in active compute path; #15 to disposition unused production/historical modules. No claim that all graphics primitives or native self-hosting are implemented. #24 takes general-purpose gaps, #15 audits combined foundations and post-bootstrap transfer, #11 reproduces these gates with self-hosted compiler/runtime.
Binding sequence now advances to #24 → #15 → #11 READY/PAUSED. #23 deferred. #11 must not be resumed without user authorization.

---

## General-purpose foundation scope correction (2026-11-24)
User clarified the goal: after self-hosting #11, DOC should be expressive enough to implement almost everything ordinarily possible in C/C++-class systems languages, not ship every such feature or application beforehand. [#24](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/24) is now the general-purpose capability-closure gate (types, dynamic computation, composition, extensible native/system effects, ABI and freestanding target foundations). Its latest binding scope narrows acceptance to genuine foundational gaps, small constructive demonstrations and native proof. Full OS/driver/timer/DMA/peripheral subsystems, library ecosystems and C++ feature parity are NOT required before #11 when implementable in DOC afterward. No arbitrary target/hardware support or weakening DOC's high-level dependency model, memory safety or no-GC/no-RC commitments. #21 remains one small 3D game with DOC-generated graphics and compute WGSL, not a graphics-engine feature-completeness exercise. #15 audits only the accepted foundations and fixes actual blockers; #11 self-hosts and revalidates them. Sequence #21 → #24 → #15 → #11 unchanged; keep #11 paused until all prerequisite gates pass and user authorizes resumption.

---

## Binding updated prerequisite sequence (2026-11-24)
User explicitly added [#24 — native system-programming and freestanding hardware capabilities](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/24) ([public tracker #4](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/4)). Required order: **#21 → #24 → #15 → #11**. Complete #21, then implement and verify #24 on main including hosted ABI/system effects and an actual freestanding bootable DOC kernel/harness. Reconcile #15 only after #21 and #24 pass, then mark #11 READY but PAUSED and notify the user. Do not automatically resume #11. Final self-hosted #11 must preserve #24's system/ABI/freestanding capabilities and prove they work without the Rust evaluator. Full GPU-only operating-system research #23 remains deferred. This supersedes prior sequencing wording, not substantive acceptance or memory-safety requirements.

---

## Binding GPU kernel source and handoff requirement (2026-11-24)

User requires DOC-authored **compute kernels as well as graphical vertex/fragment computations** before #11 resumes. WGSL is the generated backend language, not a second required authoring language. Audit the current handwritten reusable compute shader (runtime-rust/shaders/doc_reusable.wgsl), the instruction ABI and automatic scheduler, and generated graphics path. Implement real DOC-source-derived compute code generation for dependency-ready GPU workloads and reusable pure kernel functions, with compiler-derived bindings, dispatch sizing, admission and synchronization. Prefer direct specialized generated WGSL and safely cached pipelines; do not retain a permanent opcode interpreter solely to avoid compilation costs. If reusable kernel infrastructure is necessary, express portable kernel algorithms in DOC and generate its WGSL too; justify only the minimal generic platform/ABI boilerplate emitted by the compiler. Retain old shader/ABI as a test oracle until proven replacement; custom WGSL may remain optional explicit interop, never necessary for ordinary DOC GPU programming or the showcase. No arbitrary GPU execution annotation in game source, no requirement to force non-GPU-suitable effects/operations onto GPU. Preserve strict explicit GPU selection, honest automatic CPU fallback before dispatch, exact typed CPU parity, actual mixed physical GPU compute separate from rendering, atomic publication, limits and safe lifetimes. Verify generated compute and graphics on software and physical hardware with actual results, source mutation, cache/reuse and performance measurements. Ordinary DOC authors need not know WGSL syntax or bindings; no duplicate WGSL-like language. Any new primitives must have defined CPU semantics and typed IR support; #11 must preserve these in self-hosted compilation. Complete #21's single playable 3D game gate, then perform the required #15 reconciliation before declaring readiness for #11.

---

## Binding scope correction — one small 3D game, not separate 2D and 3D showcases (2026-11-24)

User explicitly selects **basic 3D only** for the graphical game-engine validation. The 3D game must be a coherent playable game built using the DOC engine itself, not a standalone host-language demo, with DOC-authored scene, geometry, gameplay, materials, lighting and simple physics/physical effects. Reuse or adapt Radar Chase gameplay if helpful, but present genuine 3D geometry, perspective/orthographic camera as appropriate, depth-tested occlusion, movement and collision/physical effects, basic lighting and animation. A rotating mesh alone is insufficient. Keep it small; cover as many existing engine capabilities as practical, including entities/prefabs/resources, input, fixed steps, spawn/despawn, queries, score/win, save/restore/replay, optional audio, failure safety, automatic CPU/GPU computation, typed assets. Provide meaningful general-purpose primitives and generated WGSL from typed DOC functions, not a game-specific shader template or WGSL syntax wrapper. No manually authored shader required for this showcase; use minimal reusable WebGPU platform bindings and shader ABI, no game logic in Rust/WGSL. Preserve old 2D code/tests as regression evidence (no destructive removal needed), but **do not spend effort completing a separate 2D showcase or porting its shader**. The expanded graphics, general-purpose, physical GPU and proof requirements below remain binding, interpreted for the 3D game rather than two games. Verify actual surface presentation + readback in software CI and separate physical GPU rendering/compute with exact revision; require CPU oracle, actual mixed independent dependency work, depth/lighting/physics pixel/state checks, deterministic replay, failure and resource tests. #11 remains paused until this passes and user authorizes resumption; #11 must reproduce the accepted 3D game and generated WGSL in the final native self-hosted realization. No editor or automated art pipeline required.

---

## Binding expanded graphics and general-purpose validation gate — 2026-11-24

User explicitly expands active #21 before resuming #11. Goal: useful native DOC graphics and GPU programming, not a mechanical alternative spelling of WGSL. Keep WebGPU and WGSL as backend standards; do not reinvent GPU APIs, shader validation, window systems or asset formats. DOC must let ordinary users describe and compose graphical computation without WGSL syntax, manually declaring bindings, workgroups, or rendering pipelines. Domain knowledge (geometry, shading math, coordinate spaces) is still needed where appropriate. Custom WGSL can remain an explicit, validated low-level escape hatch, not a dependency of the showcase.

- [ ] DOC-authored declarative scene and geometry data, shape/color/material/transform/camera and graphical behavior, linked to typed dependency states, reusable pure functions and typed assets. Use small composable primitives, not a bespoke high-level scene editor, a new shading language, or graphics-only special cases masquerading as general DOC. Ordinary graphics logic must live in DOC, not in hardcoded Rust or authored WGSL.
- [ ] Typed DOC-to-WGSL lowering for useful vertex/fragment and compute operations from DOC definitions; compiler derives stage interface, resource layout/bindings, pipeline/dispatch metadata and safe numeric/typed admission. Reuse existing frontend/typed IR and compute lowering. Establish CPU reference semantics, explicit unsupported diagnostics, bounded resources, deterministic code generation, valid shader modules and real GPU execution. Add only coherent general-purpose numeric/vector/matrix/collection primitives where necessary; don't require authors to know WGSL names or syntax. Do not weaken checked semantics, automatic placement or publication. Record language/IR changes so #11 compiles the SAME language.
- [ ] Existing Radar Chase full 2D graphical game uses DOC-authored rendering/scene definitions and actually generated WGSL, not the previous handwritten game shader as its active path. Keep all 15-action replay/16-frame, typed state, entity/radar, GUI input, resize, HUD/animation, checkpoint/audio and failure coverage; prove actual surface presentation plus GPU pixel readback and separate real automatic mixed compute. Include another independently authored graphics example and negative/mutation tests proving generated shaders respond to source changes.
- [ ] Basic 3D rendering interface: DOC-defined vertices/mesh indices, transforms, camera/projection, depth testing/occlusion and basic material/color, a small visible rotating/overlapping geometry showcase, generated vertex/fragment WGSL, actual pixels and depth-order proof. Low-level reusable interface is acceptable; no requirement for advanced shadows, photorealism, complex physics, visual editor or generated art. Use text-based assets or reproducible geometry source.
- [ ] Validate real Linux x86_64 CPU and software WebGPU CI, actual window presentation under Xvfb with input/resize tests, and separate physical GPU offscreen rendering/compute (Kaggle) with exact source/binary provenance, actual pixel/readback parity and appropriate software/physical labels. Do not call offscreen physical rendering a physical desktop presentation. Preserve #22 automatic unannotated mixed CPU/GPU compute in real game; graphics dispatch is not compute scheduling evidence. Test missing device/failure, resource lifetime, bounded retirement, no partial game publication. Document measurements and known limits.
- [ ] Audit general-purpose gaps before #11: distinguish semantics from device constraints, support composable GPU functions over useful numeric/geometry data without WGSL boilerplate, preserve no user lifetimes/borrow checking/GC/RC controls and final production no-GC/RC policy. No forced full WGSL feature parity or general-purpose graphics framework reinvention; if abstraction fails, document concrete blockers rather than claiming full flexibility. Require reviewed language/IR/runtime coverage, exact accepted revision, reproducible actual evidence on both issues, then confirm readiness to user. Keep #11 paused until readiness is demonstrated and user authorizes resumption. Final #11 must reproduce accepted 2D and 3D graphics and DOC→WGSL from self-hosted native binaries. Editor and automated art remain deferred.

This supersedes earlier 2D-only/3D-deferred wording, not historical #10/#22 acceptance. Work only on rtu0/doc2 main.

---

## Active 2D graphical game validation (2026-11-24)
User explicitly paused #11 and resumed the narrow graphical-game portion of #21. Use existing Radar Chase DOC game and the existing WebGPU/WGSL + winit window adapter. No new gameplay in Rust/WGSL, no replacement engine, no authored placement hints. Validate actual window, keyboard movement/spawn/despawn/pause/restart, rendered player/coin/wall/live entities, score/HUD and animation, typed game state and deterministic full replay parity against terminal game. Retain automatic dependency-ready CPU/GPU compute, separate from graphics; verify actual mixed compute and software vs physical adapter labels. Require actual render pixel/frame evidence, not compilation or GPU compute alone. Exercise resize and error handling; maintain existing headless tests. Software Xvfb presentation and physical offscreen rendering/compute are distinct; do not call them physical desktop presentation. Work directly on public rtu0/doc2 main only. Preserve #11 work at 9c17a46696a60994e0042d20da177e639a836e75; do not continue compiler or self-hosting until user authorizes after graphical validation. #10/#22 historical acceptance unchanged. Full editor, generated assets, 3D remain deferred. Final #11 must also preserve the validated graphical game in the self-hosted native realization.

## Historical issue comments copied from the prior development repository

Original authors, dates and links are retained below; these are archival copies, not newly executed validation.

---

**rtu0 — ** ([original comment](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/3#issuecomment-7123554457))

## Graphical implementation started
User explicitly selected WebGPU graphics. [3134629](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/3134629158c714c0c98bf4c447877df44663b01f) extends the existing winit/wgpu window host to Radar Chase with all 16 recurrence carry fields, automatic compute, E/X spawn/despawn, read-only DOC scene/entity/radar fields, shape rendering and score/status display. Original DOC game unchanged. Replay waits for presentation of each logical state including epoch zero; optional --verify-pixels renders a matching offscreen target and reads actual GPU-produced bytes, classifying all grid cell centers against the stable DOC scene. [4ea8612](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/4ea861207acff10a1c5b3be386f1696c55571ae9) repairs the initial invalid workflow literal regex; [exact CI](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45337690763) queued. No graphical pass yet. CI must diff all 48 frame/entity/radar lines with terminal CPU oracle and verify 16 logical presentations/pixel checks plus real mixed software-WebGPU computation. Further acceptance: real keyboard events/resize, failure/rollback, physical WebGPU offscreen rendering of the actual game on Tesla T4 with real mixed compute and readback, and provenance distinguishing virtual/physical desktop. Capture a usable screenshot artifact if feasible. #11 checkpoint 9c17a46 preserved with 2/2 native CI passed; compiler development paused, do not resume automatically. Full editor, generated art, 3D deferred.

---

**rtu0 — ** ([original comment](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/3#issuecomment-7124450050))

Current #21 source status: generated mesh vertex/fragment WGSL at 649c710f14da2c4691dde891b591aaa4bd89426c passed both Linux jobs (https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45341082692). Generated specialized compute replaces active handwritten interpreter at e674a759e9f8b4e86befbf0e89366d04a2fc07f4; run 45341942246 stopped before compilation because static scope guard still demanded obsolete reusable-interpreter log. Corrected guard at e02bd94d0ecf0cad4658a38b0397b53757754f33, requiring generated compute source and actual creation/reuse evidence while preserving provider/hardware checks. New CI not yet verified. Full 3D game, exact physical generated-kernel/render evidence, #24 and #15 remain outstanding. No readiness claim.

---

**rtu0 — ** ([original comment](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/3#issuecomment-7124644084))

Direct implementation session (not just scheduled handoff): 
- 321dca6f25083884bfda63d1d389e42574e7d491: reusable Scene3d ABI driven by typed DOC source declarations; actual Radar Chase 3D mesh assets, DOC camera/lighting and jump/gravity/floor contact, reused engine gameplay/automatic radar compute; CPU tests at 45344593695/job/138276109825 passed.
- ebc1720720a3e462c4d8e88501339ad26eaf2dfc: generic MeshRenderer with indexed depth rendering, actual window and offscreen replay/readback executable doc-scene3d, exact-CI artifact added to physical Kaggle controller and raw 3D proof verifier. Offline fixture corrected at b7948c92.
- 2348a05e24b47d7e2b2681a4dc5889d3f0fb9f1a: private candidate projection validation before recurrence publication.
- 684ce77a0adbfb5c40c77be7302e443a129f57fa: typed checkpoints, restored static scene authority, DOC audio cue WAV effects. Exact Linux CPU job https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45345296787/job/138278307001 passed (all four new scene tests including replay worker parity, generated WGSL parse, invalid projection rollback, checkpoint/audio equivalence; 27 offline controller tests). WebGPU job https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45345296787/job/138278698837 is still in progress; no software/physical full-game rendering acceptance claim yet. Keep CI running on exact current SHA; remaining requirements include actual interactive input/resize and stronger depth/lighting game evidence, device failure proof, physical 3D replay+generated compute, then #24 and #15. #11 stays paused.

---

**rtu0 — ** ([original comment](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/3#issuecomment-7124878666))

Continuation: 684ce77a exact software WebGPU job https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45345296787/job/138278698837 actually passed the 17-frame window and offscreen 3D replays (DOC_SCENE3D_SOFTWARE_REPLAY_PASS), CPU parity, actual 16 mixed frontiers (9 CPU + 134 GPU ready states each), 8–14 distinct colors in window frames, and generated pipeline reuse. Full job failed later due to obsolete expectation of one generated pipeline for parallel_frontier.doc, which has 128 independent derives and one dependent folded state. bc9ad8dff82a1d790c18bafcead9598120f91784 corrects both CI and physical checks to require both generated pipelines and real dispatches. 23f7a53937995f270f5a44f833b5168d7e4e2d41 adds test-only actual game mesh depth ordering, three expected face colors, fragment DOC source mutation, jumping/landing, repeated rendering and invalid inputs, X11 keyboard/resize via xdotool, and physical exact-binary proof/failure rollback. fcedb889915ea86f8476dc8c2b4f5b341cd97087 repairs the literal regex in that workflow. Latest full candidate CI https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45347136352 is pending/in progress; these stronger checks are not claimed passed yet. #21 stays open pending exact-revision full CPU/software/physical evidence and remaining review. Do not begin #24 implementation or #15 clean-pass ledger ahead of acceptance.
